headline: 20-of-24 traveled. The 88 rushing yards have to.
dek: Kansas City is 3-0 after a 24-10 win at Hard Rock Stadium, and the tape that actually matters — 88 rushing yards, 3-of-7 on third down, 25:39 with the ball — now goes to the Raiders on Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT.
videoHook: Mahomes was 20-of-24 and Kansas City still lost the clock in Miami. That is the film Las Vegas is watching, and that is the problem this show is about.
theEdge: ESPN FPI at 72.6 percent and DraftKings hanging Chiefs -5.5 on a 46.5 total is a road-favorite number, not a bye; Polymarket’s 8.6 percent Super Bowl price is what a 3-0 team gets when it wins 24-10 while losing first downs, third downs, and nearly nine minutes of football.

storyline.lede: The 2026 Chiefs are unbeaten, and the Miami tape is the first one that feels like a warning instead of a launch. Patrick Mahomes carved Hard Rock Stadium at 20-of-24 for 246 yards and two touchdowns, Kenneth Walker III added 70 yards and a score on 18 carries, and Kansas City still walked out with 18 first downs against 19, 3-of-7 on third down, 88 rushing yards as a team, and 25:39 of possession against Miami’s 34:21. That is a 24-10 win with last year’s footprints on it, and the next Sunday is already a division road game that will not grade on completion percentage.
body: Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy got the start they wanted. Travis Kelce ripped a 48-yarder down the middle on the opening series, Kansas City punched a 10-yard touchdown, and a 5-yard score early in the second quarter made it 14-7. Rodriguez took the other way, and a defense that had to keep answering because the offense could not stay on the field. Arrowhead Pride’s rapid reaction put it plainly — after two games that looked reinvented, this one looked like the frustrating 2025 club, and it still won (https://www.arrowheadpride.com/kansas-city-chiefs-analysis/211452/rapid-reaction-last-years-chiefs-almost-come-out-close-call-dolphins).

Steve Spagnuolo’s unit did the quiet winning. L’Jarius Sneed forced and recovered a Malik Willis fumble in the second quarter, George Karlaftis intercepted Willis in the fourth, and Miami’s 329 yards and 8-of-16 on third down never became more than 10 points. Nick Bolton led the tackle sheet with 11. That is complementary football in the scoreboard column and a problem in the clock column: you cannot ask that front to live in 34-minute games every week and also ask it to travel to Allegiant Stadium.

Patrick Mahomes already said the quiet part to a young roster. That message now has a date stamp: Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT, at the Raiders, with the Chargers already three games back in the West according to Arrowhead Addict (https://arrowheadaddict.com/chargers-nightmare-start-is-already-giving-chiefs-massive-afc-west-edge?utm_source=RSS). The division will not wait for the run game to remember the Indianapolis tape (152 rushing yards, 37:00 of possession). It will play the Miami tape until Kansas City rips it up.

lastGameReview.label: Week 3 · Sun, Sep 27 · 12:00 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: The Dolphins out-gained nobody — 329 yards to 334 — but they won the downs and the clock.

analysis.body: The opening sequence was the version of this offense people came to see. Mahomes hit Travis Kelce for 48 yards to the Miami 19, and Kansas City cashed a 10-yard touchdown for 7-0. Miami answered with a 3-yard touchdown to tie it at 7-7, and Kansas City went back in front 14-7 on a 5-yard touchdown. Those were not empty calories: Mahomes later dropped a 17-yarder to Thornton, a 17-yarder to Xavier Worthy, a 24-yarder to Noah Gray, and a 34-yarder to Rashee Rice. He was accurate and on time. He was not, for long stretches, complementary to a run game that finished with 88 team rushing yards.

The second quarter is the film session. Miami turned it over on downs, Kansas City answered by burning a short-yardage chance — Hunter Nourzad reported eligible, Walker took it up the middle for no gain at the Miami 12, turnover on downs. Rodriguez at the Miami 29. You cannot call that a complementary sequence. You can call it the 2025 habit: explosives and negative plays living in the same quarter.

Spagnuolo won the scoreboard anyway. Karlaftis picked Willis two snaps of game clock later. Harrison Butker then missed a 50-yarder wide left, which did not change the result and did put a messy stamp on a messy close. Miami still ran 119 yards and sat on the ball for 34:21. Ten points is the grade. The snap count is the homework.

takeaways.title: Mahomes was efficient. The offense was not durable.
takeaways.body: 20-of-24 for 246 and two touchdowns is a winning quarterback line. 3-of-7 on third down, 18 first downs, and 25:39 of possession is not a winning drive chart against a division opponent. The Raiders will play the chart, not the rating.

takeaways.title: The defense took the ball and still had to live in a long game.
takeaways.body: Sneed forced and recovered a Willis fumble, Karlaftis intercepted Willis, and Miami scored 10. That is a Spagnuolo win. It is also 34:21 of Dolphins possession and 119 rushing yards allowed, which is how a 10-point game still feels like a grind.

takeaways.title: Red zone and short yardage left points on the grass.
takeaways.body: Walker was stuffed on fourth down at the Miami 12. Those are the snaps Bieniemy has to clean before Allegiant Stadium makes them expensive.

whatWorked: Mahomes’ accuracy (20-of-24, 246 yards, two passing touchdowns) and the deep-middle/deep-sideline shots to Kelce (48), Gray (24), and Rice (34).
Takeaways: Sneed forcing and recovering Willis’ fumble, Karlaftis intercepting Willis with Chris Jones in the play.
whatDidnt: Team rushing (88 yards) after 152 against Indianapolis, with Walker at 70 on 18 carries.

currentState.lede: Kansas City is 3-0 with wins over Denver (31-10), Indianapolis (33-30), and Miami (24-10), and the season has already split into two tapes: the 523-yard, 37:00 possession explosion against the Colts, and the 334-yard, 25:39 grind in Miami. The Raiders game is where the staff decides which tape is the identity.

workOn.title: Early-down run identity
workOn.body: Walker’s 18 carries for 70 yards did not drag the team total past 88. Against Indianapolis the club ran for 152. Las Vegas will load the box until Bieniemy proves inside zone is a threat, not a tell.

workOn.title: Third down and the clock
workOn.body: 3-of-7 on third down is how you lose 34:21 to 25:39 even when you win 24-10. A division road game punishes that math. The Chiefs have to stay on schedule so Spagnuolo is not rationing a front that just played a long one.

workOn.title: Finishing inside the 10
workOn.body: Walker got nothing on fourth down at the 12. Those are the points a one-score AFC West game will not give back.

thinkAbout.title: Is this still the 2025 offense in a 3-0 coat?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Pride’s rapid reaction said last year’s Chiefs almost came out in Miami (https://www.arrowheadpride.com/kansas-city-chiefs-analysis/211452/rapid-reaction-last-years-chiefs-almost-come-out-close-call-dolphins). The 6-11 hangover is not a record this year. It is a style. The Raiders will tell us if Reid has actually buried it.

thinkAbout.title: How loud does Mahomes have to be for a young roster?
thinkAbout.body: He already told them they cannot relax (https://www.arrowheadpride.com/kansas-city-chiefs-news/211488/patrick-mahomes-reminds-young-chiefs-team-cant-relax). The next test is whether that message hits before kickoff at Allegiant or after a slow first quarter.

thinkAbout.title: Market versus the West
thinkAbout.body: ESPN FPI sits at 72.6 percent for Las Vegas and DraftKings has Kansas City -5.5 on 46.5. Polymarket still prices the Chiefs at 8.6 percent to win the Super Bowl. That gap is the season in one number: favored this week, untrusted for January, until the run game and the clock catch up to the record.

gamePlan.lede: Week 4 is the first AFC West road game of the 3-0 start: Kansas City at the Raiders, CBS, Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT. Miami just showed every division opponent the blueprint — run it, convert third down, sit on the ball, and make Mahomes beat you in a short-possession game.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City’s leverage is still Mahomes, Kelce, Rice, and a Spagnuolo call sheet that just produced a Sneed fumble recovery and a Karlaftis interception while holding Miami to 10. Las Vegas’ leverage is the same one Miami used: physical AFC West snaps, a crowd that will live on third-and-long, and a Chiefs run game that just posted 88 yards. If Walker and the interior cannot win first down, the Raiders do not have to blitz Mahomes to bother him — they can just make him operate left-handed on the road. If Kansas City establishes inside zone, play-action and boot become the same explosives that opened Miami (Kelce 48, Gray 24, Rice 34) without handing Las Vegas the clock.

keys.title: Get to 100 as a team on the ground
keys.body: Walker had 70 of Kansas City’s 88 at Miami. The Colts game (152 rushing yards, 37:00) is the target. Inside zone on early downs is how you keep the Raiders from turning this into a passing-down hunt.

keys.title: Do not donate short yardage
keys.body: The Nourzad-eligible Walker stuff at the Miami 12 cannot travel. Reid has to have a quarterback sneak, a gap scheme, or a play-action boot ready on fourth-and-1 so a division game does not stall at the 12.

keys.title: Make Las Vegas one-dimensional, then steal it
keys.body: Bolton just played an 11-tackle game against 119 rushing yards. Spagnuolo should live in Cover-2 while the run is a threat, then zone-blitz Jones and Karlaftis the first time the Raiders get greedy on early downs. The Miami takeaways were the win. Repeat that, do not repeat the 34:21.

keys.title: Explosives without the pick
keys.body: The Rodriguez interception on the deep middle to Rice is the one Mahomes has to leave in Florida. Four verts and the deep over are still live against a split-safety look — just not into a bracket when the Chiefs are already ahead.

script: Open in 12 personnel and run inside zone at Walker until Las Vegas puts an eighth man in the box.
Play-action boot off that look to Kelce and Noah Gray; Mahomes was surgical rolling and throwing in Miami (20-of-24).
Mesh to Rice/Kelce on second-and-medium, the down Kansas City has to stay out of third-and-7.
Walker spacing screen when the Raiders pin their ears back; punish the same aggressive rush Miami tried to live on.
Cover-2 on early downs to take away the deep shot and let Bolton and the second level rally.
Zone blitz Jones/Karlaftis with a dropping end on second-and-long — the look that helped produce the Willis interception.

nextGame.label: Week 4 · Sun, Oct 4 · 3:25 PM CT
nextGame.note: First AFC West road game of a 3-0 start, Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT — the Miami clock tape against a division crowd.

spotlight.title: Mahomes was the adult in the room
spotlight.body: The Raiders game is whether the huddle heard him.

spotlight.title: Walker’s volume is not yet an identity
spotlight.body: 18 carries, 70 yards, one touchdown is honest work. 88 team rushing yards is not a Reid/Bieniemy identity. Las Vegas is where 18 carries have to mean 100 for the club, not 70 for the lead back.

spotlight.title: Rice and Kelce still travel
spotlight.body: Kelce’s 48-yarder opened the scoring drive and, per Arrowhead Pride, he iced it with a touchdown catch in traffic. That two-man game is the easiest answer if the run stalls again.

spotlight.title: Takeaways saved a messy offense
spotlight.body: Sneed forced and recovered Willis’ fumble. Karlaftis intercepted Willis with Jones on the play. Bolton had 11 tackles. Ten points allowed is the headline; 34:21 and 119 rushing yards are the fine print Spagnuolo will not ignore.

spotlight.title: The division is already tilting
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Addict notes the Chargers’ nightmare start has them three games behind Kansas City before the Week 6 meeting (https://arrowheadaddict.com/chargers-nightmare-start-is-already-giving-chiefs-massive-afc-west-edge?utm_source=RSS). Dropping a 3-0 road favorite in Las Vegas is how you donate that edge back.

spotlight.title: Buy the QB, sell the clock
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Addict’s Week 3 stock report framed a closer-than-expected win with plenty to buy and sell (https://arrowheadaddict.com/chiefs-stock-report-after-week-3-win-reveals-plenty-to-buy-sell?utm_source=RSS). The buy is Mahomes’ efficiency. The sell is 25:39 of possession traveling into a division stadium.

matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes (20/24, 246, 2 TD, 1 INT) with Kelce and Rice
matchups.note: The Miami completion rate travels. The Rodriguez pick on the deep middle to Rice is the one snap Las Vegas will try to bait again.

matchups.unit: Walker and the Chiefs OL vs. Raiders front
matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III (18-70-1) and a line that managed 88 team rush yards
matchups.opponent: Raiders defensive front, AFC West box counts
matchups.note: Indianapolis proved this line can hit 152. Miami proved it can get stuck at 88. Whichever show up decides whether Mahomes plays with a play-action leash.

matchups.unit: Spagnuolo pass rush vs. Raiders OL
matchups.chiefs: Chris Jones, George Karlaftis, simulated pressure
matchups.note: Karlaftis already took one from Willis. Jones was in the picture. A division quarterback on the road is where Spagnuolo’s zone blitz has to be more than a changeup.

matchups.unit: Bolton and the run fit vs. Raiders ground game
matchups.chiefs: Nick Bolton (11 tackles) and the second level
matchups.opponent: Raiders run game attacking the same 119-yard look Miami found
matchups.note: Ten points allowed hides 119 rushing yards and 34:21. If Las Vegas can do the same, Kansas City’s 3-of-7 third down becomes a long afternoon.

matchups.chiefs: Rashee Rice (7-88) and Travis Kelce (48-yarder plus the icing score)
matchups.opponent: Raiders linebackers in man and hook zones
matchups.note: Mesh and the deep middle are still Kansas City’s cleanest answers when the run is stuck. Las Vegas has to pick a player to help, and Reid will throw at the other one.

xsandos.title: Walker downhill, first-down identity
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, opening script at Allegiant, 12 personnel vs. the Raiders
xsandos.why: Kansas City just ran for 88 as a team in Miami after 152 against Indianapolis. Walker’s 18-70-1 is volume without a dent. Las Vegas will sit on Mahomes until inside zone forces a safety down. This is how Bieniemy keeps the Chiefs out of the 3-of-7 third-down hole that handed Miami 34:21.
xsandos.coaching: Walker has to press the line and pick one cut — the Miami fourth-down stuff at the 12 was a no-gain because the crease never got defined. Creed Humphrey and the guards owe him a vertical double; Reid should keep Nourzad-as-eligible in the short-yardage package but not as a give-up run into a loaded front.

xsandos.title: Boot off the run fake
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 after a Walker inside-zone look, Raiders overhang chasing the back
xsandos.why: Mahomes was 20-of-24 because he was throwing on time, not because Kansas City was under center grinding. Play-action boot is how you turn 88 rushing yards into the same explosives that hit Kelce for 48 and Gray for 24 without asking the line to win a five-man protection on obvious pass.
xsandos.coaching: Mahomes has to sell the mesh point and get his eyes to Kelce on the bootleg flat-to-corner before the Raiders’ backside end can flatten. Gray trails as the late dig. Do not scramble into a throwback; the Rodriguez interception came when Kansas City got greedy down the middle.

xsandos.title: Rice/Kelce rub vs. man
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-5 / 3rd-and-4 vs. Raiders man coverage, Rice aligned inside
xsandos.why: Rice’s 7-for-88 and Kelce’s ability to win in traffic (Arrowhead Pride’s icing touchdown) are the man-beating answers if Las Vegas dares to play the run with extra bodies. Miami already showed that Kansas City will go 3-of-7 when the easy access throws disappear. Mesh puts a ball in Mahomes’ hand before the rush can pin him.
xsandos.coaching: Rice has to rip across Kelce’s hip and not balloon the crossing route. Kelce sets the rub, then sits if the linebacker jumps Rice. Walker is the checkdown — the outlet Mahomes did not need often in Miami (20-of-24) but will need on the road if the first crosser is trailed.

xsandos.title: Walker screen, punish the heat
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-7 or 3rd-and-5 when Las Vegas walks a safety down and rushes five
xsandos.why: Kansas City cannot live in dropback on the road after a 25:39 possession game. A Walker spacing screen turns the Raiders’ aggressiveness into the missing explosive run (team rush was 88; Walker had 70 of it between the tackles). It also protects a young group Mahomes already told not to relax.
xsandos.coaching: The left side of the line has to get out in space — no holding downfield, no lunging. Walker must set the rush with a pass-pro hint, then get north. Rice and Worthy block the first white jerseys in the perimeter; this is not a hero ball for Mahomes, it is a possession snap.

xsandos.title: Spagnuolo two-deep, take the shot away
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 / 2nd-and-long vs. the Raiders, safeties split, Bolton in the hole
xsandos.why: Cover-2 is how Spagnuolo keeps a division quarterback from that same over route while Bolton (11 tackles) and the linebackers rally to a run game that just posted 119 on this defense. With Chamarri Conner inactive in Miami, the safe shell also protects a shuffled secondary on the road.
xsandos.coaching: Corners have to funnel, not gamble — L’Sneed already made his splash by forcing and recovering the Willis fumble, not by jumping a double move. Safeties split the hashes and drive on the catch. Bolton fits the alley; do not let Las Vegas turn early downs into the clock game Miami just played.

xsandos.title: Simulated heat, drop the end
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-8 vs. the Raiders, Jones inside, Karlaftis showing, linebacker adding
xsandos.why: Karlaftis intercepted Willis on a short throw with Jones on the play; that is the payoff of Spagnuolo making a quarterback throw into a disappearing lane. Las Vegas will see the Miami 8-of-16 third-down tape and try to stay ahead of the chains. A zone blitz on second-and-long is how Kansas City gets a negative snap without emptying the coverage behind Bolton.
xsandos.coaching: Show five, rush four. Jones collapses the pocket; Karlaftis either comes or drops into the throwing lane he just undercut in Miami. The adding linebacker has to be the fifth rusher or the hook defender — not both, not late. Sneed stays home after the fumble recovery; do not blitz him into a glance route.

coaching.topic: Reid / Bieniemy vs. the Miami drive chart
coaching.detail: The openers worked (10-yard touchdown, 5-yard touchdown, Kelce’s 48-yarder). Allegiant is not the week to get cute on fourth-and-1 or to abandon inside zone after two stuffed runs.

Ten points and two takeaways (Sneed fumble force/recovery, Karlaftis interception) is a win. 119 rushing yards and 34:21 is a warning. Cover-2 on early downs and the zone blitz on second-and-long is how he keeps Las Vegas from copying Miami’s clock.

He already told a young roster it cannot relax after the Miami win. The staff’s job is to script a first quarter that looks like the 7-0 start, not like the 25:39 possession line, so that speech is not required again at 0-0 in the fourth.

injuries.note: Officially ruled out for the Dolphins game; the secondary played Miami without him.
Listed among the inactives at tackle for Chiefs-Dolphins.
Tight end inactive against the Dolphins.
Elevated from the practice squad, then listed among those who would not play vs. Miami.

personnel.detail: Kenneth Walker III handled 18 carries for 70 yards and a touchdown in Miami.

Kansas City elevated linebacker Cole Christiansen and defensive end Tyreke Smith for Miami (https://www.arrowheadpride.com/kansas-city-chiefs-news/211395/chiefs-elevate-2-practice-squad-players-for-week-3). Depth on the second level remains a live issue after Bolton’s 11-tackle workload.

Arrowhead Addict, citing Adam Schefter, says the Giants have interest in Fields and that prying him out of Kansas City is another matter (https://arrowheadaddict.com/giants-may-want-justin-fields-but-prying-him-from-chiefs-is-another-matter?utm_source=RSS). That is a roster subplot, not a Week 4 game plan.

strategies: Commit to inside zone with Walker on the first two series in Las Vegas until the Raiders put an eighth man in the box.
Use play-action boot to Kelce/Gray as the constraint off that run, the same way the 48-yard Kelce shot opened Miami.
Keep Rice in the mesh/crosser game on second-and-medium so Kansas City is not living at 3-of-7 again.
Script a real short-yardage package — sneak, gap, or boot — so the Walker stuff at the Miami 12 does not become a division-game habit.
Play Cover-2 on early downs to erase the deep middle Miami hit for 42 to Dulcich, and let Bolton rally.
Zone-blitz Jones and Karlaftis on second-and-long to recreate the throwing lane Karlaftis undercut for the interception.
debates: Is 3-0 with 25:39 of possession a launch, or is it the 2025 offense with a better quarterback line?
How many carries does Walker need in Las Vegas before Bieniemy is allowed to go empty?
Did Spagnuolo actually fix the pass rush, or did Willis just donate a fumble to Sneed and a pick to Karlaftis?
Should Kansas City treat -5.5 at the Raiders as a must-cover, or is 3-0 already enough cushion with the Chargers three back?
Is Mahomes’ ‘cannot relax’ speech a leadership win, or a tell that the young roster still needs to be talked into road games?

runOfShow.talkTrack: Mahomes went 20-of-24, Kansas City won 24-10, and Miami still had the ball for 34:21. Tell them the Raiders game on Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT is about the clock, not the completion percentage.
Then the tape: Kelce 48, Walker stuffed at the 12, Sneed force-and-recover, Rodriguez pick on Rice, Gray to the 8 that became a field goal, Rice 34, Karlaftis INT, Butker 50-yard miss.

3-0, two tapes — 523 yards and 37:00 against Indianapolis versus 334 and 25:39 in Miami. Mahomes told the young team it cannot relax. Chargers already three back. Polymarket 8.6 percent still treating this like a sample.

Four offense: inside zone, play-action boot, mesh, Walker screen. Two defense: Cover-2 to take away the deep shot, zone blitz to recreate the Karlaftis lane. Tie every card to Las Vegas, not to a generic call sheet.
Favorite at -5.5, FPI 72.6 percent, 46.5 total. Win first down, get the team past 88 rushing yards, do not donate short yardage, steal a possession. Division road game, CBS, Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT.
Leave them with the clock question and the 2025 hangover question. Tease Week 6 vs. the Chargers only as the West picture, then send them out looking at Allegiant, not at the 24-10 final.
